title: Remember map zoom level and focus hex across reloads
description:
The map view resets when a game is reloaded. The user has to zoom and pan back to where they were working.

Goal: persist the map viewport per game so reloading restores the previous view.

Scope:
- Persist current zoom level and the focused/centered hex
- Restore them when the same game is loaded again
- Fall back to the current default view when no saved state exists (e.g. first load of a game)

Acceptance criteria:
- Reloading a game restores the zoom level and centered hex from the previous session
- Viewport state is stored per game, so switching between games does not mix up views

title: Map forgets known-but-never-occupied hexes once no unit can see them
description:
When a unit moves away, the map stops showing hexes that were known only from that unit's line of sight. Only the hex the unit itself occupied earlier remains on the map; the surrounding 6 hexes (e.g. ocean hexes seen from a fleet jump but never entered) disappear.

Expected: once a hex has been observed in any report, it stays on the map as known terrain (with the data from the last turn it was observed), even when no unit can currently see it.

Actual: only hexes a unit actually occupied are remembered; adjacent observed-only hexes are dropped when they leave current visibility.

Acceptance criteria:
- Hexes observed from an adjacent unit remain visible on the map after the unit leaves
- Remembered hexes show the terrain and data from the most recent turn they were observed
- Currently visible vs remembered hexes remain distinguishable (see ah-rgp)

title: Option to keep the long order format when exporting orders
description:
Exported orders come out in the short format only. The server's own unit description — name,
flags, weight, capacity, skills and what the unit can study, wrapped over as many `;` lines as it
takes — is dropped the moment a report's template becomes an editable document
(`stripUnitComments` in `packages/shared/src/ordersDocument.ts`, called once from
`documentFor` in `packages/shared/src/orderDraft.ts:113`), and `exportOrders`
(`packages/shared/src/workspace/AppShell.tsx:1526`) writes that stripped document straight out.

Dropping the descriptions from the editor was deliberate (#37): the unit panel already says all of
it, and on a unit with no orders yet the description is the whole block. But the exported file is
read elsewhere — kept as a record of the turn, diffed against the next one, or read by a human
without this application in front of them — and there the long format is what makes a bare
`unit 793` legible:

```
unit 793
;Three of Five (793), behind, revealing faction, leader [LEAD]. Weight:
;  10. Capacity: 0/0/15/0. Skills: observation [OBSE] 1 (35), force
;  [FORC] 1 (35), pattern [PATT] 1 (30), spirit [SPIR] 1 (30), gate
;  lore [GATE] 1 (30), fire [FIRE] 1 (30), combat [COMB] 3 (180). Can
;  Study: earthquake [EQUA], force shield [FSHI], energy shield [ESHI],
;  spirit shield [SSHI], magical healing [MHEA], farsight [FARS], mind
;  reading [MIND], weather lore [WEAT], earth lore [EART], necromancy
;  [NECR], demon lore [DEMO], illusion [ILLU], artifact lore [ARTI].
@study obse
```

So the option belongs on the export, not on the editor: the descriptions stay out of the panel the
player writes in, and go back into the file on the way out when asked for.

## Scope

- An option on the orders export that puts the server's long-format unit descriptions back into the
  exported text. Default off, so today's output is unchanged unless the player asks.
- The descriptions are recovered from the report's own template (`parsed.ordersTemplate`), matched
  per `unit` block, rather than kept in the document — the document must stay as it is, or the
  editor regains the clutter #37 removed.
- Each unit's description is written directly under its `unit` line, above the player's orders, in
  the server's own wrapping, byte for byte as the report carried it.
- Units the template has no description for (a unit formed this turn by the player) simply get
  none; the export must not fail or invent one.
- The player's own `;` notes in the draft are untouched and not duplicated.
- The same option and the same output on both shells — web download and desktop save alike.

## Out of scope

- Any change to what the editor shows, or to `stripUnitComments` at seed time.
- The `Orders Template (Long Format):` banner and the region `;*** ... ***` banners — this is about
  unit descriptions only.
- The map export in `crates/core/src/report/export.rs`, which is a separate path.
- Reformatting or re-wrapping descriptions; they go out as they came in.

## Validation

- `pnpm run check` and `cargo test` (or `pnpm run check` alone if the change stays in TypeScript).
- A unit test over the committed turn 71 fixture: export with the option on, and every `unit` line
  that has a description in the template is followed by exactly those `;` lines, in that order.
- The same export with the option off is byte for byte what is exported today.
- Round trip: an export written with the option on, imported back as a draft, seeds a document with
  the descriptions stripped again — no accumulation.
- A smoke test exercising the checkbox from the orders panel, on web and desktop-shell.
- Manually: export a turn with the option on, and read the file — a leader's eight-line description
  should be intact and correctly indented.
acceptance_criteria:
The orders export offers an option, default off, that writes the server's long-format unit descriptions into the exported file.
With the option off the exported text is byte for byte what is exported today.
With the option on, every unit whose template block carried a description has those ';' lines directly under its 'unit' line, verbatim and in order, above the player's orders.
A unit with no description in the template exports without one and without error.
The player's own ';' notes are neither dropped nor duplicated.
Re-importing an export written with the option on seeds a document with the descriptions stripped, so they do not accumulate.
The option and its output are the same on the web download and the desktop save.

title: Make terrain of undiscovered hexes more visible on the map
description:
Undiscovered (not yet explored) hexes render their terrain image so heavily whitened/faded that the terrain type is not distinguishable at a glance. There are thin differences in the image background, but they are too subtle.

Goal: make it clear at a glance what terrain an undiscovered hex has, while still keeping a clear visual distinction between discovered and undiscovered hexes.

Ideas to consider:
- Reduce the whitening/desaturation amount for undiscovered hexes
- Keep the fade but add a stronger terrain-colored tint
- Use a distinct marker (outline style, hatching, reduced opacity instead of whitening) for the discovered/undiscovered distinction instead of washing out the terrain

Acceptance criteria:
- Terrain type of an undiscovered hex is recognizable at a glance in all map themes
- Discovered vs undiscovered hexes remain visually distinguishable

title: Max number of units settable from the units-in-hex pane
description:
It should be possible to increase/decrease the number of units that are shown in the units-in-hex pane by clicking a + or - located to the right on the top bar of the pane. There shall also be a text indicating what the max units shown are, as this may be more than the hex currently has.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The units-in-hex pane's top bar carries + and - controls on its right-hand side.
- Clicking + or - raises or lowers the maximum number of units listed, and the list updates immediately.
- The top bar shows the current maximum, including when the hex holds fewer units than that.
- The chosen maximum survives a reload.

title: Toggle badges on/off in the map display
description:
It should be possible to toggle different badges on/off in the map display to reduce cluttering.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Each kind of badge drawn on the map can be turned on and off independently.
- The map redraws immediately when a badge kind is toggled.
- The chosen set of visible badges survives a reload.

title: Commit a second turn so multi-step routes can be proved on real data
description:
## Summary

Commit a second real turn for one faction, so that routes longer than one step can be proved against
real data rather than only against synthetic corridors.

## Problem

Issue #8 built a map that accumulates across turns, and it works: the core merges remembered regions
with the current report, the current turn wins where they disagree, and both platforms store and
read back region sightings. All of that is unit-tested.

None of it can be demonstrated end to end, because the repository holds exactly one report per
faction: neworigins-3.0.0-f73-t2.rep for faction 73 and neworigins-3.0.0-f95-t71.rep for faction 95.

A single report cannot support a route longer than one step. It describes the hexes the faction
stood in and names their neighbours, but a named hex describes no exits of its own, so the graph
stops at the fringe. With the committed fixtures, every route the planner produces is one step.

Multi-step, multi-month, road and flight behaviour is therefore covered only against small synthetic
reports built in the tests. Those are honest tests, but they are our own fixtures rather than the
game's output, and they cannot catch a disagreement between what we think a report says and what one
actually says.

Fabricating a second turn was deliberately avoided during #8: inventing game data and committing it
as a fixture would make every test built on it worthless as evidence.

## Scope

- Commit a genuine second turn for faction 95, ideally adjacent in time to turn 71
- Add an acceptance test that imports both turns and plans a route crossing ground the later report
  does not describe
- Extend the smoke suite so the multi-step case is exercised in a browser, not only in the core

## Acceptance criteria

- Two turns of one faction are committed under tests/fixtures/reports
- A test plans a route of more than one step over the accumulated map, with a cost read from the
  reports by hand
- The stale map state is exercised, since it becomes reachable only once a hex is remembered from an
  earlier turn than the current one

## Validation

    cargo test --workspace
    pnpm run check

## Dependencies / Links

- Main issue: #1
- Follows: #8

## Note

This one needs a human: the report has to come from a real game.

title: Plan sea movement for fleets
description:
## Summary

Plan sea movement: routes for units aboard a fleet, emitting SAIL rather than MOVE.

## Problem

The planner handles land movement only. A unit standing in an ocean hex - which is what a unit
aboard a fleet looks like in a report - is refused with "the sea is in the way", and so is any
destination across water. That is correct for what #8 built, and useless for a faction that sails.

The rules make sailing a second system rather than a variation:

- A fleet has its own speed, stated per ship on the data page: a Longship moves 4 hexes per month, a
  Raft 2, a Galleon 4
- "For a fleet to enter any region only costs one movement point", so the terrain premium that
  applies to riding and walking units does not apply at sea
- Sailing needs a total of N levels of sailing skill among the crew, stated per ship
- A fleet has a cargo capacity, which the scraper already records as cargoCapacity
- Guards behave differently: a fleet enters a guarded region and is then stopped, where a land unit
  is prevented from entering at all

## Scope

- A Sail movement mode, with speed taken from the ship rather than from the unit
- Flat terrain cost at sea, per the quoted rule
- Recognising that a unit is aboard a fleet it can actually sail, including the skill requirement
- Emitting SAIL orders rather than MOVE
- Refusing a sea route with a named reason when the crew cannot sail the ship

## Out of scope

- Combat at sea
- Building or repairing ships

## Acceptance criteria

- A unit aboard a fleet can be given a sea route with a cost and a month breakdown
- A crew without the sailing skill the ship requires is refused with that as the reason
- Land units are unaffected

## Notes

Two loose ends from #8 belong here. MovementMode has no Sail variant, deliberately. And
crates/core/src/movement/mode.rs has a can_swim function that nothing outside its own test calls -
this ruleset's water rule exempts only flight from needing a ship, so swimming currently decides
nothing; it should either be used here or deleted.

## Dependencies / Links

- Main issue: #1
- Out of scope of: #8

title: Import lots of reports
description:
There are plenty of old Borg reports that could be imported to the code base to potentially be used for testing. This issue should cover importing them into the code base in a structured way and they should be used by later issues.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The Borg reports are committed under a documented location in the repository.
- File naming encodes game, faction and turn so a test can select a report without opening it.
- A short document records where the reports came from and what they may be used for.

title: Turn-to-turn diffs for units, regions, and orders
description:
## Summary

Compare two imported turns of a game and see what changed: units gained/lost/moved, region changes, and how the orders differ.

## Problem

The app keeps every imported turn in storage, but the player can only ever look at the latest one. Between turns the real questions are "what changed since last month?" and "what did I order last time?" — today that means opening two report text files side by side.

## Scope

- An API to enumerate the imported turns of a game (`listImportedTurns` through core-persistence, the WASM and Tauri adapters, and the shared `CoreClient`), since today only "a known turn number" or "latest" can be loaded.
- Loading a second turn alongside the current one for comparison (the app currently holds exactly one parsed report in memory).
- A diff view for a chosen turn pair surfacing adds/removes/changes for units, regions, and orders.

## Out of scope

- Diffing more than two turns at once, or cross-game comparison.
- Changes to report parsing or order validation.

## Acceptance criteria

- The user can pick two imported turns of the current game.
- The diff view lists units added, removed, and changed between the pair.
- The diff view lists region changes between the pair.
- The diff view shows how the orders drafts differ between the pair.

## Validation

- Import two consecutive turn reports with known differences; open the diff view and verify each known difference is surfaced and nothing is falsely reported.
- Vitest coverage for the diff computation modules; a Playwright smoke walk of the diff view on both web and desktop-shell projects.

## Dependencies / Links

- Broken out of issue 9 (Productivity UX), where it was originally a scope bullet; deferred to its own deliverable.
- Storage substrate already exists: `imported_turns` table keyed by game/faction/turn in `crates/core-persistence`.

title: Load multiple reports
description:
It shall be possible to load multiple reports in one go. The application shall then look at the headers of all reports to figure out in which order the reports shall be loaded. It shall be possible to load both your own and allies reports in one go.

While we are at it, the menu option for loading orders shall be changed to "Import".

## Acceptance Criteria

- Several report files can be selected and imported in one action.
- The application reads the turn number from each report header and loads them in turn order, regardless of the order they were selected in.
- Own-faction and ally reports can be imported together in the same action.
- The menu option for loading reports reads "Import".

title: Record beads CLI traps in the beads-workflow skill
description:
Three beads behaviours bit during the #126 migration and are not obvious from the CLI help. Record them in the beads-workflow skill so the next session does not rediscover them.

- The pre-commit auto-export can write a stale snapshot: a commit picked up a JSONL still containing a throwaway bead that had already been deleted.
- `bd config set` accepts unknown keys silently, so a mistyped key reads as success; probing also rewrote a commented-out default in `.beads/config.yaml` and stripped its trailing newline.
- The `owner` field is taken from `git config user.email` at creation and has no override; `--actor` sets `created_by` only, and `--assignee` is a separate field.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `.claude/skills/beads-workflow/SKILL.md` carries a section covering all three behaviours.
- The export trap names the verification command that catches it.
